question: The national song of India, 'Vande Mataram', is an excerpt taken from the novel _____ written by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay.
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Anand Math**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anand Math**

 
 
• The famous book ‘Anand Math' was authored by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee.
 
• The book was written in 1882.
 
• Anandamath takes the reader back to Bengal in the clutches of the famine, the backdrop of the pre-independence struggle, and the turmoil of human lives caught in this time frame. 
 
• It is considered one of the most remarkable works of the Bangla language and Indian literature.
 
• Through the book, Bankim Chandra Chatterjee also gave us the song ‘VandeMataram’which became the rallying call for rebels.
 
• The first two stanzas eventually became the National song of India.
 
• One of the gems of Indian Literature, ‘Anandmath’ carries a deep sentiment of nationalism which was the essence of the freedom struggle.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Vande Mataram

 
 
• The author of Vande Mataram is Bankim Chandra Chatterjee. 
 
• He wrote it in the 1870s, which was later included in his 1881 novel Anandamath.
 
• It played a vital role in the Indian independence movement, first sung in a political context by Rabindranath Tagore at the 1896 session of the Indian National Congress. 
 
 

 
• Bankim Chandra Chatterjee or Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay:

 
 
• He was an Indian novelist, poet, and journalist.
 
• He was the composer of Vande Mataram, originally in Sanskrit, personifying India as a mother goddess and inspiring activists during the Indian Independence Movement.
